current_disclosures.section: Risks Related to Our Business, Operations, and Industry
current_disclosures.summary: Micron's gross margins are influenced by manufacturing cost decreases, product mix, process complexity, yields, capacity utilization, and input costs, with underutilization leading to higher per gigabit costs.

comparisons.peer_summary: Failure to achieve expected manufacturing yields, caused by design, process, or packaging technology failures, could increase per-unit costs, harm gross margins, and result in product delivery delays or lost sales.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies explicitly link manufacturing yield failures or inefficiencies to increased per-unit costs and adverse impacts on gross margins. Micron identifies yield issues and facility underutilization as factors limiting cost reduction, while AMD states that low yields or manufacturing inefficiencies at third-party foundries can result in increased per-unit costs that adversely impact gross margin.

sentences.text: • increasing complexity of our product portfolio, which may impact operational costs;

In addition to the impact of our average selling prices, our gross margins are dependent, in part, upon continuing decreases in per gigabit manufacturing costs achieved through improvements in our manufacturing processes and product designs.

Semiconductor manufacturing yields are a result of product design, process technology and packaging technology, which is typically proprietary to the manufacturer, and low yields can result from design failures, packaging technology failures, process technology failures or a combination of some or all of these.

Any decrease in manufacturing yields could result in an increase in per unit costs, which would adversely impact our gross margin and/or force us to allocate our reduced product supply amongst our customers, which could harm our relationships and reputation with our customers and materially adversely affect our business.

comparisons.peer_summary: Gross margin depends on product mix, price erosion, acquisitions, capacity utilization, and commodity prices; shifts in sales mix, competition, and demand fluctuations can negatively impact margins, while supply imbalances may create unsustainable high margins.
comparisons.comparison: Both Micron and Broadcom disclose that gross margins are significantly driven by manufacturing capacity utilization and the risk of underutilization or supply imbalances. Micron explicitly links facility underutilization to higher per-gigabit costs and margin deterioration, while Broadcom identifies capacity utilization as a key dependency for gross margin and notes that supply imbalances (both shortages and oversupply) can lead to volatile or unsustainable margin outcomes.

sentences.text: • higher manufacturing costs per gigabit due to fabrication facility underutilization, lower wafer output, and insufficient volume to run new technology nodes to achieve cost optimization.
Our gross margin is dependent on a number of factors, including our product mix, price erosion, acquisitions we may make, level of capacity utilization and commodity prices.
Conversely, periods of robust demand that create a supply imbalance can lead to higher gross margins that may not be sustainable over the longer term.

comparisons.peer_summary: Risks in developing next-generation nodes include timing delays, lower yields, and higher costs due to advanced equipment. Delays can cause missed customer design windows, larger die sizes, and supply constraints, while new nodes typically have higher depreciation and lower yields than mature nodes.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies highlight that manufacturing yields and process technology transitions directly impact unit costs and gross margins. Micron states that factors like product complexity and fabrication facility underutilization limit its ability to reduce per-gigabit costs, whereas Intel details how lower-than-anticipated manufacturing yields and delays in next-generation process nodes increase product costs and adversely affect gross margins.

sentences.text: • increasing complexity of our product portfolio, which may impact operational costs;

In addition to the impact of our average selling prices, our gross margins are dependent, in part, upon continuing decreases in per gigabit manufacturing costs achieved through improvements in our manufacturing processes and product designs.

Risks inherent in the development of next-generation process technologies include production timing delays, lower-than-anticipated manufacturing yields, longer manufacturing throughput times, failure to achieve expected performance, power, and area improvements, and product defects and errata (deviations from published specifications).

Lower manufacturing yields and longer manufacturing throughput times, compared to previous process nodes, can increase our product costs, adversely affect our gross margins, and contribute to manufacturing supply constraints.

comparisons.peer_topic: Demand estimation errors and financial consequences
comparisons.peer_summary: Failure to accurately estimate customer demand has led to mismatches between supply and demand, resulting in product shortages, excess inventory, and significantly harmed financial results. Underestimating demand can lead to inadequate capacity from foundry partners, failure to fulfill orders, and lost revenue, while overestimating demand can result in an inability to reduce inventory commitments, price reductions, inventory write-downs, cancellation penalties, and increased product costs from supplier price hikes, all negatively impacting gross margins.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address how mismatches between supply and demand impact financial results and margins, though the mechanisms differ. Micron focuses on manufacturing-side constraints (yield, underutilization, complexity) limiting cost reductions, while NVIDIA focuses on demand estimation errors leading to product shortages or excess inventory that harm financial results. NVIDIA explicitly links overestimation of demand to price reductions and write-downs affecting gross margins, similar to how Micron links operational inefficiencies to margin deterioration.

sentences.text: In addition to the impact of our average selling prices, our gross margins are dependent, in part, upon continuing decreases in per gigabit manufacturing costs achieved through improvements in our manufacturing processes and product designs.
• higher manufacturing costs per gigabit due to fabrication facility underutilization, lower wafer output, and insufficient volume to run new technology nodes to achieve cost optimization.
All of these factors may negatively impact our gross margins and financial results.
This mismatch has resulted in both product shortages and excess inventory, has varied across our market platforms, and has significantly harmed our financial results.

peer_results.rationale: QCOM's retrieved candidates focus on competitive pricing pressures reducing average selling prices (avgo_2024_1A_D068 is Broadcom, not QCOM; QCOM's candidates are qcom_2024_1A_D077 and qcom_2024_1A_D046). While QCOM mentions margin impact from pricing, the core driver is external competition and ASP erosion rather than internal manufacturing cost/yield/underutilization dynamics which are the primary focus of Micron's disclosure. QCOM's manufacturing candidate (qcom_2024_1A_D046) discusses yield risks generally but does not explicitly link them to gross margin in the same direct causal way as Micron or AMD/INTC in the provided texts, making it less directly comparable to the specific 'Gross Margin Drivers and Cost Reduction Challenges' topic which blends margin impact with specific operational cost levers like underutilization and yield optimization. The match with AMD, INT, AVGO, and NVDA is stronger due to explicit 'gross margin' and 'yield/cost' linkage.
